docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §10 (general pre-auth responses <= 128 B — challenges, rejections, errors; TM-6 revised)
description: The 128 B pre-auth response boundary: the three pre-auth response shapes (AuthChallenge, AuthResult(202), AuthResult(204)) with their exact sizes — all without any detail field.
preconditions: Pre-auth responses: AuthChallenge, pairing/auth refusals, pre-auth errors — stable codes only, NO detail (spec §4.2).
The sole exception to the 128 B rule is a successful PairingResponse (<= 320 B, see limits/pairing-response-320b).
The bound applies to the whole framed response (u32 BE length prefix included); the asserted sizes below are framed sizes.
assertions: Every step's framed size must be <= 128 bytes (asserted via size_bounds); the largest here is AuthChallenge at 47 B.

No detail field may be present in any pre-auth response — even a short one (spec §4.2; TM-6 as revised 2026-11-12 withdrew the nonce-gated blanket exemption: admission is gated per mode instead, not by response size).
These are the exact bytes of the frames used by control.auth-happy-path / error-202 / error-204.
